payload.public_message: Greetings partners. G-Corp brings proprietary chip architecture critical to this joint venture. Due to standalone licensing alternatives, our firm has a firm walk-away value of $450,000. To launch discussions productively, we propose an equitable distribution that respects baselines and shares the surplus: $500,000 for G-Corp, $250,000 for Yang Industries, and $250,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Thank you, G-Corp, for laying out your position. Our firm contributes manufacturing capacity that is essential to getting this product to market, so a $250k share does not reflect our contribution. We are willing to move toward a balanced split. We table a counter: G-Corp $400,000, Yang Industries $350,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $250,000. We are open to refinements that reflect each party's real contribution.

Chang-Liu's cloud services are essential to the venture's delivery and ongoing operation. To give this negotiation a credible path to agreement, we propose G-Corp $450,000, Yang Industries $350,000, and Chang-Liu $200,000. This recognizes each party's stated position while ensuring the venture can move forward.

Yang Industries appreciates the movement toward a workable split. Our manufacturing capacity is central to delivery, and 350k is the floor we can consider. We propose a small adjustment: G-Corp 425,000, Yang Industries 375,000, Chang-Liu 200,000. It moves only the G-Corp share, and it better reflects the manufacturing role. We are willing to close quickly on a split close to this.

To move toward a binding agreement, we propose a split that recognizes G-Corp's stated baseline and Yang Industries' stated floor, while preserving a meaningful share for Chang-Liu's essential cloud services. We are ready to finalize on this basis.

While we appreciate Chang-Liu structuring an offer around our $450,000 baseline, an allocation of exactly $450,000 yields zero surplus for G-Corp over our standalone licensing alternative, giving us no commercial incentive to commit. A viable joint venture must share the created surplus with all partners rather than expecting G-Corp to contribute critical architecture for zero net benefit. We propose $470,000 for G-Corp, $340,000 for Yang Industries, and $190,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services, ensuring every party captures real value from this partnership.

To demonstrate our commitment to reaching an agreement that works for all parties, G-Corp is prepared to meet Yang Industries at their stated floor of $350,000, while requesting only a modest $10,000 concession from Chang-Liu Cloud Services. An allocation of $460,000 allows G-Corp a minimal $10,000 surplus above our outside option—the minimum required for our board to justify participating in this joint venture rather than pursuing our independent licensing route. We propose $460,000 for G-Corp, $350,000 for Yang Industries, and $190,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We invite both partners to ratify this balanced structure.

Yang Industries accepts the current proposal: G-Corp $460,000, Yang Industries $350,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $190,000. This split respects the manufacturing contribution we have consistently identified as central to delivery. We urge Chang-Liu to ratify so the venture can be finalized this round.
Chang-Liu accepts G-Corp’s proposal of $460,000 for G-Corp, $350,000 for Yang Industries, and $190,000 for Chang-Liu. We are ready to finalize the binding agreement.
